# Code Review Report

## Review Summary

This branch removes the legacy dependency-injector, LangChain provider, and application-layer RAG service, then updates the docs to describe the OpenCode-first runtime. The cleanup direction is sound, but the branch leaves one hard breaking change in the packaged CLI path and two stale provider-contract issues that will mislead users and configs after the LangChain removal.

**Files Reviewed:** 29  
**Findings:** 1 Critical, 2 Warning, 0 Suggestion

## Findings

### Critical Findings

[C-01] Installed `ai-story-writer` command is now a guaranteed runtime failure  
Category: Correctness  
Severity: Critical  
File: src/presentation/cli/main.py  
Lines: 6-24  
Description: The PR replaces the active CLI with a stub that always raises `NotImplementedError` at [src/presentation/cli/main.py](src/presentation/cli/main.py#L17), but the packaged console entrypoint still routes through [src/setup.py](src/setup.py#L38) and [src/setup.py](src/setup.py#L39) into [src/main.py](src/main.py#L15) and [src/main.py](src/main.py#L21). Result: anyone invoking the installed `ai-story-writer` command now gets an immediate failure instead of a supported migration path. That is a breaking change in the shipped interface, not only an internal deprecation.
Suggestion: Either remove the `console_scripts` entrypoint in the same PR, or keep a compatibility wrapper that prints migration guidance and exits cleanly without throwing. If the CLI must remain installable, it should redirect to the supported OpenCode workflow rather than fail by exception.

### Warning Findings

[W-01] `ModelConfig` still accepts provider schemes that no active provider implements  
Category: Correctness  
Severity: Warning  
File: src/domain/value_objects/model_config.py  
Lines: 30-37  
Description: After deleting the LangChain provider, the active runtime only advertises `openai_compatible`/`ollama` via [src/infrastructure/providers/openai_compatible_provider.py](src/infrastructure/providers/openai_compatible_provider.py#L378), `lm_studio` via [src/infrastructure/providers/lm_studio_provider.py](src/infrastructure/providers/lm_studio_provider.py#L395), and `llama_cpp` via [src/infrastructure/providers/llama_cpp_provider.py](src/infrastructure/providers/llama_cpp_provider.py#L493). However, `ModelConfig` still validates `google`, `openrouter`, `openai`, and `anthropic` as supported providers. That leaves configuration accepting values the runtime no longer has an implementation path for, so invalid configs survive validation and fail later in harder-to-diagnose ways.
Suggestion: Tighten `valid_providers` to the providers that still have active implementations, or add replacement adapters for the removed schemes in the same PR.

[W-02] User-facing config examples still advertise removed provider schemes  
Category: Documentation  
Severity: Warning  
File: config.md  
Lines: 207-215  
Description: The updated branch documentation says the active stack now uses direct OpenAI-compatible providers and the legacy LangChain layer is gone, but [config.md](config.md#L207) through [config.md](config.md#L215) still shows `google://...` and `openrouter://...` model examples. After this PR, those examples no longer match the active provider set, so users following the documented configuration path can select models that the runtime does not actually support.
Suggestion: Replace those examples with supported `openai-compat://`, `ollama://`, `lm_studio://`, or `llama_cpp://` examples, or clearly mark the removed schemes as archived legacy syntax that is no longer supported in `src/`.

## Overall Assessment

Not ready for merge. The dependency cleanup itself is directionally correct, but the PR currently breaks the packaged CLI contract and leaves stale provider support in both validation and user-facing configuration docs. Once the console entrypoint behavior and provider contract are made consistent with the new runtime, the branch should be in much better shape.
